items.cold_note: Threshold 170. Bars: 300=140, 400=165, 500=190, 600=178, 700=163, 800=120. Only 500 (190) and 600 (178) reach 170 -> B. But the student sees only ticks 0/47.5/95/142.5/190 and no value labels. 170 sits 27.5 above the 142.5 tick (58% of the interval); 400 (165, 47% of the interval) and 700 (163, 43%) are 5-7 units below it, about 10-15% of one tick interval. 600 (178) is 8 above. Telling 165 from 170 by eye against 47.5-unit ticks is not reliable, so a careful student could read the 400 bar as at or just above 170 and defend C. The 700 bar is 2 units lower than 400, so D needs a reading error at both and is weaker. Readability concern: these ticks are too coarse for the cut that the question asks for.

second_defensible.reason: No value labels and ticks 47.5 units apart (142.5, 190). The 400°C bar (165) is 5 units below the 170 cut, about 10% of one tick interval, and the 600°C bar (178) that counts as passing is only 8 above. Against these ticks a careful student cannot tell 165 from 170, so reading 400°C as meeting the cut and choosing C is defensible from what is drawn.

items.readability_note: The key depends on whether the 400°C bar (165) and the 700°C bar (163) clear 170, and the student can only estimate heights against ticks at 0/47.5/95/142.5/190 with no gridline or tick at 170. The margins are 5 and 7 units below the cut (10-15% of one tick interval), and the 600°C bar that passes is 8 above. The ticks are too coarse for the cut the stem asks for. The data are right, but the drawn figure does not decide the key.
items.note: From the data the key is correct: 190 and 178 are >= 170, while 165, 163, 140 and 120 are not. The options are nested supersets ordered by threshold, so no free elimination without the figure. The defect is purely visual: the data were authored with near-miss values at a cut that falls between ticks. It is passage-level only in the sense that the same chart sits under every question; other items asking for coarser comparisons may be fine.
